title: Finding Record v1
description: One record per audit finding, appended once — no event stream, no fold (v0.5.0 FR13, D5, D11). Each line of specs/audits/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-<session_id_8chars>/FINDINGS.jsonl is one object validating this schema, keyed by `id`. Every property carries a custom `x-mutability` keyword — `immutable-core` (never rewritten once appended: id, pillar, severity, refs, claim, evidence) or `mutable-governance` (rewritten in place by the remediation release that dispositions it: disposition, release, reason) — THIS is the one place the two-category split is documented; core/models/findings.py never re-declares it as a second, driftable list (A13.1, mirrors A2.1/A2.10). `specs/audits/**` has one CLI writer for the governance triple (`dadaia audit disposition`, 0.4.7 FR4); a finding is APPENDED by an agent's file tools (immutable core, like an ADR), so A13.5's hand-redaction rule (evidence is the reproducible command plus a redacted one-line result, never a raw transcript) is what keeps a record clean, not a write-time seam.

id.description: `<audit-slug>-F<nnn>` — stable identifier of this finding within its audit window.

pillar.description: Which of the three audit pillars (FR14) produced this finding.

severity.description: Severity level, set when the finding is first appended.

refs.description: file:line, bug ids, commit shas, and/or release ids the claim is anchored to.

claim.description: One sentence stating what the finding asserts.

evidence.description: The reproducible command plus a redacted one-line result (A13.5) — e.g. `git show <sha> --stat -- <module> → 2 files changed, second render path added`. A `.dadaia/tmp/**` path may accompany it as a convenience pointer, never replace it.

disposition.description: Governance state, appended as `open` and rewritten in place by `dadaia audit disposition` (0.4.7 FR4). The terminal words are exactly `core.models.histo.FINDINGS_DISPOSITIONS` — one finding vocabulary; the historical `fixed` was renamed to `resolved` with zero committed FINDINGS.jsonl to migrate.

release.description: The remediation release id that dispositioned this finding — null until one does.

reason.description: Free-text rationale for the disposition — null until the finding is dispositioned.

examples.claim: fix-induced bug: the skip-detail leak rides the second render path the probe-gate fix introduced, and the probe-gate bug resolved without a structural cause
examples.evidence: git show <sha-A> -- dadaia_workspace/features/certification (second render path added); BUGS.jsonl codex-live-probe-gate-checks-presence-not-usability cause=null
